findings.title: SQL injection in migration data load
findings.body: The migration interpolates the value of `h` (a host string from `site_settings.embeddable_hosts`) directly into raw SQL: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)`. Any host containing a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) will break the statement or allow arbitrary SQL execution. Even though the input is from a trusted admin setting, the loader should sanitize/escape the value (e.g. via `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote` or `sanitize_sql_array`) or insert via the ActiveRecord `EmbeddableHost` model so the model's `before_validation` (http://, path stripping) is also applied consistently with how the rest of the app creates hosts.

findings.title: NoMethodError when updating a non-existent host
findings.body: `update` does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then calls `save_host(host)`. If no row matches the id, `host` is nil and `save_host` executes `host.host = ...` / `host.category_id = ...`, raising NoMethodError on nil and a 500 error to the admin. It also blindly `where().first` without scoping, which is a smaller concern. Guard the call, e.g. `head :not_found and return unless host`.

findings.title: Strong parameters and validation not used; NoMethodError on missing params
findings.body: `save_host` indexes straight into `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `[:category_id]`. A request without that key (or with non-hash input) raises NoMethodError instead of returning a 400/422. Use a permitted-parameters whitelist (`params.require(:embeddable_host).permit(:host, :category_id)`) and return proper validation errors. There's also no uniqueness validation on `host`, so two admins can create duplicate `embeddable_host` rows that will collide silently and confuse the `where('lower(host) = ?', host)` lookup in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on nil host
findings.body: The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')`. If `host` is nil (or non-string), `sub!` raises NoMethodError, blowing up validation instead of producing a clean validation error. Use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(/^https?:\/\//, '').sub(/\/.*$/, '')` (or guard with `return unless self.host.is_a?(String)` and a separate `presence` validation) so the user gets a normal validation message.

findings.title: Host regex too narrow; valid hosts rejected and old data won't load
findings.body: `validates_format_of :host, with: /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` requires a dot plus a 2–5 letter TLD, which rejects legitimate hosts such as `localhost`, plain hostnames without TLDs, IPv4 literals, IDN/punycode-style hosts, and any host whose TLD is longer than five letters (e.g. many real-world TLDs). More importantly, the migration's raw INSERT copies values verbatim from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting into the new table without running them through this validator, so legacy entries that don't match the regex will be silently inserted but will fail validation the moment any code tries to save them again. Add `presence` and `length` validations, broaden or replace the regex (e.g. parse with `URI`/`Addressable`), and have the migration create records through the `EmbeddableHost` model so normalization + validation are applied.

findings.title: Migration INSERTs raw, non-normalized hosts
findings.body: The data migration copies the old site-setting values straight into the table via raw SQL. The new model normalizes hosts (strips `http(s)://`, strips paths) in `before_validation`; skipping that means `http://example.com/foo` and `example.com/foo` end up as distinct rows in the new table that won't match the normalized values the runtime expects (because `record_for_host` queries with `uri.host` only). Use `EmbeddableHost.create!(host: h, category_id: category_id)` (or call the normalizer) inside the data-loading loop.

findings.title: category_id may still be 0 / DB will reject null NOT NULL column
findings.body: If both the `embed_category` site setting is missing AND the `uncategorized_category_id` row is missing or non-numeric (e.g., fresh test DBs with no settings), `category_id` stays 0 and the subsequent `INSERT ... VALUES (..., #{category_id}, ...)` writes `category_id = 0` into a `null: false` column, causing the whole migration to abort on Postgres. Also `cmd_tuples` is Postgres-specific; the migration won't run on MySQL/SQLite (it's `affected_rows`/`changes`). Guard against zero, and drop the not-null on `category_id` or default it appropriately so the migration is portable and robust.

findings.title: category fabricator definitions moved to wrong file; will break many specs
findings.body: The PR replaces the contents of `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` with the `embeddable_host` fabricator and puts the original category/diff_category/happy_category/private_category fabricators in a NEW file `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. Fabricator typically resolves `Fabricator(:category)` via the file `category_fabricator.rb`; with that file now defining `:embeddable_host` instead of `:category`, every existing test that does `Fabricate(:category)` (and the `embeddable_host` fabricator itself, which uses the bare `category` argument) will fail with `NoFabricatorDefined`. This is a broad test-suite regression. Put the category fabricators back in `category_fabricator.rb` and the embeddable_host fabricator in its own file, or rename the file to match.

findings.title: _hydrateEmbedded does not filter undefined subtype lookups
findings.body: The new array branch builds `const hydrated = obj[k].map(function(id) { return self._lookupSubType(subType, type, id, root); });`. `_lookupSubType` can legitimately return `undefined` (the `category` short-circuit aside, the doc lookup returns nothing for unknown ids / collection-absent). Storing those `undefined`s in the result array means embedded readers get `[undefined]` entries and `length` includes them — the new `store-test.js.es6` asserts `fruitCols.length` is exactly the number of valid ids, so this works only because the fixtures happen to contain every id. Use `.filter(Boolean)` after the map, or treat an undefined lookup as a failure to fully hydrate (delete `obj[k]`/don't populate the array), and add a test case where the embedded ids exceed the available collection to lock the behavior in.

findings.title: type.replace('_', '-') replaces only the first underscore
findings.body: The basePath lookup is now `type.replace('_', '-')`, but `String#replace` with a string argument only replaces the first occurrence. Any pluralized type that ends up with more than one underscore (currently none, but it's a sharp edge for future types like `foo_bar_baz`) will not match `ADMIN_MODELS`. Use `type.replace(/_/g, '-')` (regex with global flag) to be safe.

findings.title: Embedding adapter's pathFor ignores args; breaks all REST verbs
findings.body: `pathFor()` returns the static string `"/admin/customize/embedding"` and ignores `store`, `type`, and `findArgs`. That works for the single `embedding` model (a singleton at GET/PUT `/admin/customize/embedding`), but `rest.js#pathFor` is invoked for `find`, `findAll`, `update`, `createRecord`, and `destroyRecord`. Because the embedding adapter's `pathFor` returns the same URL for every verb, an accidental `findAll('embedding')` / `createRecord('embedding')` would issue a GET/PUT/POST/DELETE against the same endpoint and either be silently mis-handled by the controller or cause a confusing 404/route mismatch. Override only the verbs that actually exist (e.g. define a `find`/`update` that call the parent) or limit the resource surface area.

findings.title: Discourse.Category.findById is not synchronous; assignment never updates UI
findings.body: `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`. `findById` (and `find`) return a Promise; assigning the unresolved promise to `category` leaves the UI showing no category until a subsequent full reload. Use `Discourse.Category.findById(...).then(c => host.set('category', c))` or the sync store lookup. Additionally, `edit()` reads `this.get('host.category.id')` without guarding for nil — for a freshly created row whose `category` is null this throws, though the `editing || isNew` predicate normally hides that path.

findings.title: Controller tests are placeholders; no behavior is exercised
findings.body: The new `embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` (and `embedding_controller_spec.rb`) only assert `controller_class < Admin::AdminController`, which is a trivial Ruby constant check. They don't exercise create/update/destroy, don't test the nil-host guard, don't test the category_id fallback, don't verify `before_filter` authentication, and don't check that `save_host` serializes correctly with `rest_serializer: true`. With the bugs in the controller (NoMethodError on missing params and on missing record), the absence of real specs is exactly what lets those bugs through.

findings.title: Same placeholder-only coverage for Admin::EmbeddingController
findings.body: Identical placeholder test as `embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb`. There's no coverage of `fetch_embedding` ordering/caching, of `show` vs `update` rendering shape, or that the serializer is using the rest_serializer flag — all of which the new JS code in `admin-embedding.js.es6` and `embedding.hbs` now rely on.

findings.title: No spec for nil/blank host, or invalid hostnames
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` calls `sub!` on `host` without checking presence, and the format regex is strict. There are no specs asserting the behavior when `host` is nil, empty, contains only a scheme, or contains uppercase/path. Adding those would lock in intended behavior and catch the NoMethodError bug above.

findings.title: REST PUT response no longer propagates IDs back to store
findings.body: Pre-PR the PUT path looked like `update(...).then(function(json) { return json[typeField].id ? ... storeMap(...) : ... })` (it's gone). The new `update` adapter just returns the unwrapped payload. Combined with the changes in `store.js#update` that look up `result[type]` (note: stores now use the raw camelCase type, not `typeField`), any consumer that previously got an updated record back will now see a payload without going through the identity-map store. Not broken for this PR's editor (which sets `.category` manually) but it is an API contract change for the rest adapter.

findings.title: Silent category fallback to nil when no EmbeddableHost matches
findings.body: Previously an imported topic was forced into `SiteSetting.embed_category` regardless; now `eh.try(:category_id)` means a `TopicEmbed.import` for a URL that doesn't resolve to any `EmbeddableHost` record yields a topic with `category: nil`, which then gets snapped to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` by `Topic#ensure_topic_has_a_category`. That's a data-integrity change (imported topics land in Uncategorized instead of the configured embedding category), and it's worth either documenting explicitly or rejecting the import when no host matches (matching the controller-side `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` policy).
